periods = data["periods"]
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
trans_edges = [tuple(e) for e in data["network"]["trans_edges"]]

cost_purchasing = data["costs"]["purchasing"]
cost_inventory = data["costs"]["inventory"]
cost_waste = data["costs"]["waste"]
cost_lost_sales = data["costs"]["lost_sales"]
cost_transshipment = data["costs"]["transshipment"]

stores = ["Store1", "Store2", "Store3"]
dcs = ["DC1", "DC2"]

m = gp.Model()
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

T_set = range(periods)
max_sl = max(shelf_life.values())

Q = m.addVars(products, T_set, lb=0, name="Q")
I = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in T_set:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

Trans = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (src, dst) in trans_edges:
        for t in T_set:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                Trans[p, src, dst, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"Trans_{p}_{src}_{dst}_{t}_{r}")

sales = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in stores:
        for t in T_set:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

W = m.addVars(products, locations, T_set, lb=0, name="W")
L = m.addVars(products, stores, T_set, lb=0, name="L")

for p in products:
    for t in T_set:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

for l in locations:
    for t in T_set:
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * I[p, l, t, r] 
                       for p in products 
                       for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            <= cold_capacity[l],
            name=f"cold_cap_{l}_{t}"
        )

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for t in T_set:
        trans_out = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, "Plant", dst, t, sl] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == "Plant")
        m.addConstr(I[p, "Plant", t, sl] == Q[p, t] - trans_out, name=f"plant_fresh_{p}_{t}")

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for t in range(periods - 1):
        for r in range(1, sl):
            trans_out_rplus1 = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, "Plant", dst, t, r+1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == "Plant")
            avail = I[p, "Plant", t, r+1] - trans_out_rplus1
            m.addConstr(I[p, "Plant", t+1, r] == avail, name=f"plant_age_{p}_{t}_{r}")

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for t in T_set:
        trans_out_1 = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, "Plant", dst, t, 1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == "Plant")
        m.addConstr(W[p, "Plant", t] == I[p, "Plant", t, 1] - trans_out_1, name=f"plant_waste_{p}_{t}")

for dc in dcs:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            inflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, dc, t, sl] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == dc)

            m.addConstr(I[p, dc, t, sl] == inflow - outflow, name=f"dc_fresh_{p}_{dc}_{t}")

for dc in dcs:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in range(periods - 1):
            for r in range(1, sl):
                inflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, dc, t, r+1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == dc)
                outflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, dc, dst, t, r+1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == dc)
                avail = I[p, dc, t, r+1] + inflow - outflow
                m.addConstr(I[p, dc, t+1, r] == avail, name=f"dc_age_{p}_{dc}_{t}_{r}")

    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            inflow_1 = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, dc, t, 1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == dc)
            outflow_1 = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, dc, dst, t, 1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == dc)
            m.addConstr(W[p, dc, t] == I[p, dc, t, 1] + inflow_1 - outflow_1, name=f"dc_waste_{p}_{dc}_{t}")

for store in stores:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            inflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, store, t, sl] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == store)
            m.addConstr(I[p, store, t, sl] == inflow - sales[p, store, t, sl], name=f"store_fresh_{p}_{store}_{t}")

for store in stores:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in range(periods - 1):
            for r in range(1, sl):
                inflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, store, t, r+1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == store)
                avail = I[p, store, t, r+1] + inflow - sales[p, store, t, r+1]
                m.addConstr(I[p, store, t+1, r] == avail, name=f"store_age_{p}_{store}_{t}_{r}")

for store in stores:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            inflow_1 = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, store, t, 1] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == store)
            m.addConstr(W[p, store, t] == I[p, store, t, 1] + inflow_1 - sales[p, store, t, 1], name=f"store_waste_{p}_{store}_{t}")

for store in stores:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                inflow_r = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, src, store, t, r] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if dst == store)
                m.addConstr(sales[p, store, t, r] <= I[p, store, t, r] + inflow_r, name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{store}_{t}_{r}")

for store in stores:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, store, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            demand_at_store = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[store]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + L[p, store, t] == demand_at_store, name=f"demand_{p}_{store}_{t}")

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, sl + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

for (src, dst) in trans_edges:
    for p in products:
        sl = shelf_life[p]
        for t in T_set:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                if src == "Plant":
                    m.addConstr(Trans[p, src, dst, t, r] <= I[p, src, t, r] + Q[p, t] * (1 if r == sl else 0), 
                               name=f"trans_avail_{p}_{src}_{dst}_{t}_{r}")
                else:
                    inflow = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, s, src, t, r] for (s, d) in trans_edges if d == src)
                    m.addConstr(Trans[p, src, dst, t, r] <= I[p, src, t, r] + inflow, 
                               name=f"trans_avail_{p}_{src}_{dst}_{t}_{r}")

purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in T_set)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_inventory[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - (sales[p, l, t, r] if l in stores else 0) - 
                         gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, dst, t, r] for (src, dst) in trans_edges if src == l))
    for p in products for l in locations for t in T_set for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_waste[p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in T_set)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p, store, t] for p in products for store in stores for t in T_set)

transshipment_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_transshipment * Trans[p, src, dst, t, r]
    for p in products for (src, dst) in trans_edges for t in T_set for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transshipment_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

The network is an explicit three-echelon chain consisting of a plant, distribution centers, and retail stores. Customers are never backordered: store demand that cannot be met from store inventory is lost and penalized.

- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

- Demand occurs only at store nodes according to demand_share (Store1=30%, Store2=40%, Store3=30%). Upstream nodes (Plant, DCs) do not face direct customer demand.
- For each product, location, and period, inventory reflects previous stock, production or inbound shipments, outbound shipments, sales at stores, and waste, and must remain non-negative.

- T[p,src,dst,t,r] ≥ 0: transshipment quantity (CONTINUOUS)
- sales[p,l,t,r] ≥ 0: sales from inventory with r remaining (CONTINUOUS)
- W[p,l,t] ≥ 0: waste (CONTINUOUS)
- L[p,l,t] ≥ 0: lost sales (CONTINUOUS)

**Constraints:**

1. **Production capacity:** Q[p,t] ≤ production_cap[p,t]

2. **Cold storage capacity:** ∑_p cold_usage[p] * ∑_r I[p,l,t,r] ≤ cold_capacity[l]

3. **Fresh inflow at Plant:** I[p,Plant,t,SL[p]] = Q[p,t]

4. **Inventory balance for non-Plant locations (fresh):**
   I[p,l,t,SL[p]] = ∑_{src:(src,l)∈E} T[p,src,l,t,SL[p]]

5. **Aging dynamics (for r = 1 to SL-1):**
   I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] - ∑_{dst:(l,dst)∈E} T[p,l,dst,t,r+1] + ∑_{src:(src,l)∈E} T[p,src,l,t,r+1]

6. **Waste:** W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] - ∑_{dst} T[p,l,dst,t,1]

7. **Sales availability:** sales[p,l,t,r] ≤ I[p,l,t,r] - ∑_{dst} T[p,l,dst,t,r]

8. **Demand satisfaction at stores:**
   ∑_r sales[p,l,t,r] + L[p,l,t] = demand[p,t] * demand_share[l]

9. **No sales at non-store locations:** sales[p,l,t,r] = 0 for l ∉ S

**Objective:**
Minimize: ∑_{p,t} cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p,t]
        + ∑_{p,l,t,r≥2} cost_inventory[p] * (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r] - outbound_T)
        + ∑_{p,l,t} cost_waste[p] * W[p,l,t]
        + ∑_{p,l,t} cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p,l,t]
        + ∑_{p,src,dst,t,r} cost_transshipment * T[p,src,dst,t,r]

## STEP 3: GENERATE GUROBI CODE

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
import json

# Data is pre-defined
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
T_periods = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
cost_purchasing = data["cost_purchasing"]
cost_inventory = data["cost_inventory"]
cost_waste = data["cost_waste"]
cost_lost_sales = data["cost_lost_sales"]
cost_transshipment = data["cost_transshipment"]
trans_edges = [tuple(e) for e in data["trans_edges"]]

stores = ["Store1", "Store2", "Store3"]

# Build outgoing and incoming edge dictionaries
outgoing = {l: [] for l in locations}
incoming = {l: [] for l in locations}
for src, dst in trans_edges:
    outgoing[src].append(dst)
    incoming[dst].append(src)

# Create model
m = gp.Model("multiechelon")
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Decision variables
# Q[p,t]: production at Plant
Q = m.addVars(products, range(T_periods), lb=0, name="Q")

# I[p,l,t,r]: inventory at start of period t with r periods remaining
I = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods + 1):  # Need t+1 for dynamics
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# T_ship[p,src,dst,t,r]: transshipment
T_ship = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for src, dst in trans_edges:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                T_ship[p, src, dst, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"T_{p}_{src}_{dst}_{t}_{r}")

# sales[p,l,t,r]: sales at stores
sales = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# W[p,l,t]: waste
W = m.addVars(products, locations, range(T_periods), lb=0, name="W")

# L[p,l,t]: lost sales (only at stores)
L = m.addVars(products, stores, range(T_periods), lb=0, name="L")

# Constraints

# 1. Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in range(T_periods):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# 2. Cold storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in range(T_periods):
        m.addConstr(
            gp.quicksum(cold_usage[p] * gp.quicksum(I[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
                        for p in products) <= cold_capacity[l],
            name=f"cold_cap_{l}_{t}"
        )

# 3. Initial inventory is zero (t=0)
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, SL + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# 4. Fresh inflow at Plant from production
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for t in range(T_periods):
        m.addConstr(I[p, "Plant", t, SL] == Q[p, t], name=f"fresh_plant_{p}_{t}")

# 5. Fresh inflow at non-Plant locations from transshipment
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        if l != "Plant":
            for t in range(T_periods):
                inbound_fresh = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, src, l, t, SL] for src in incoming[l]) if incoming[l] else 0
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, SL] == inbound_fresh, name=f"fresh_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 6. Aging dynamics: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] - outbound + inbound
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL):  # r from 1 to SL-1
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, l, dst, t, r + 1] for dst in outgoing[l]) if outgoing[l] else 0
                inbound = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, src, l, t, r + 1] for src in incoming[l]) if incoming[l] else 0
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] - outbound + inbound,
                    name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# 7. Waste: items with r=1 that aren't sold or shipped become waste
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            outbound_r1 = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, l, dst, t, 1] for dst in outgoing[l]) if outgoing[l] else 0
            m.addConstr(
                W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] - outbound_r1,
                name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# 8. Sales availability: can only sell what's available after outbound shipments
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, l, dst, t, r] for dst in outgoing[l]) if outgoing[l] else 0
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r] - outbound,
                    name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# 9. No sales at non-store locations
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        if l not in stores:
            for t in range(T_periods):
                for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                    m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] == 0, name=f"no_sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# 10. Demand satisfaction at stores
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in stores:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# 11. Transshipment availability: can't ship more than available
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for src, dst in trans_edges:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                m.addConstr(T_ship[p, src, dst, t, r] <= I[p, src, t, r], name=f"trans_avail_{p}_{src}_{dst}_{t}_{r}")

# Objective function
obj = gp.LinExpr()

# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in range(T_periods):
        obj += cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p, t]

# Inventory holding cost: charged on end-of-period inventory for r >= 2
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(2, SL + 1):  # r >= 2
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T_ship[p, l, dst, t, r] for dst in outgoing[l]) if outgoing[l] else 0
                obj += cost_inventory[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] - outbound)

# Waste cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            obj += cost_waste[p] * W[p, l, t]

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in stores:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            obj += cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p, l, t]

# Transshipment cost
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for src, dst in trans_edges:
        for t in range(T_periods):
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                obj += cost_transshipment * T_ship[p, src, dst, t, r]

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
Locations are connected in a directed ring, mimicking a truck route that visits each location in a fixed cycle. Inventory can only move along the ring edges, and storage capacities are tightened so that the chosen routing structure affects feasibility and cost. Demand is local and exogenous at each node, and unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The transshipment network in the JSON forms a directed cycle: DC1鈫扗C2鈫扗C3鈫扗C4鈫扗C5鈫扗C1. Inventory can be shipped only along these ring edges.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. Capacities are scaled to 80% of normal values.
- For each product, location, and period, inventory reflects previous stock, local production, inbound ring shipments, outbound ring shipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Demand at each location is met from local inventory and inbound ring shipments; there are no shortcuts across the ring.
- Inventory that moves further along the route must pass through intermediate locations in sequence.
- Lead times for ring shipments are effectively zero in this archetype, and substitution behavior is as encoded.
- The objective is to minimize total cost (aggregating purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs) while respecting the ring network structure and tighter storage capacities.

      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] + ship_in - ship_out,
                            name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1], name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r], name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Demand satisfaction: sum_r sales[p,l,t,r] + L[p,l,t] = demand[p,t] * demand_share[l]
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        total_storage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * I[p, l, t, r]
            for p in products
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
        )
        m.addConstr(total_storage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_{l}_{t}")

# Ship only what's available (can't ship more than inventory minus sales)
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                ship_out = gp.quicksum(ship[p, l, l_to, t, r] for (l_from, l_to) in ring_edges if l_from == l)
                m.addConstr(ship_out <= I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r], name=f"ship_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Initial inventory at t=0 for r < SL must be 0 (no pre-existing aged inventory)
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, sl):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# Objective
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)

# Holding cost on end-of-period inventory (I - sales) for r >= 2
holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_inventory[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])
    for p in products
    for l in locations
    for t in periods
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_waste[p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

transship_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_transshipment * ship[p, l_from, l_to, t, r]
    for p in products
    for (l_from, l_to) in ring_edges
    for t in periods
    for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transship_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(

    for p in products
    for l in locations
    for t in periods
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["lost_sales"][p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

trans_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["transshipment"] * ship[p, src, dst, t, r]
    for p in products
    for (src, dst) in trans_edges
    for t in periods
    for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + trans_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

Business narrative:
Locations are connected in a directed ring, mimicking a truck route that visits each location in a fixed cycle. Inventory can only move along the ring edges, and storage capacities are tightened so that the chosen routing structure affects feasibility and cost. Demand is local and exogenous at each node, and unmet demand is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- The transshipment network in the JSON forms a directed cycle: DC1鈫扗C2鈫扗C3鈫扗C4鈫扗C5鈫扗C1. Inventory can be shipped only along these ring edges.
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. Capacities are scaled to 80% of normal values.
- For each product, location, and period, inventory reflects previous stock, local production, inbound ring shipments, outbound ring shipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Demand at each location is met from local inventory and inbound ring shipments; there are no shortcuts across the ring.
- Inventory that moves further along the route must pass through intermediate locations in sequence.
- Lead times for ring shipments are effectively zero in this archetype, and substitution behavior is as encoded.
- The objective is to minimize total cost (aggregating purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs) while respecting the ring network structure and tighter storage capacities.

  "return_rate": {"SKU_Basic": 0.0, "SKU_Premium": 0.0, "SKU_ShortLife": 0.0},

  "costs": {"lost_sales": {"SKU_Basic": 50.0, "SKU_Premium": 80.0, "SKU_ShortLife": 40.0}, "inventory": {"SKU_Basic": 1.0, "SKU_Premium": 1.5, "SKU_ShortLife": 1.0}, "waste": {"SKU_Basic": 2.0, "SKU_Premium": 3.0, "SKU_ShortLife": 2.0}, "fixed_order": 0.0, "transshipment": 0.5, "purchasing": {"SKU_Basic": 10.0, "SKU_Premium": 20.0, "SKU_ShortLife": 15.0}},

}
'''
data = json.loads(json_str)

# Extract data
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
T = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
costs = data["costs"]
trans_edges = data["network"]["trans_edges"]
sub_edges = data["network"]["sub_edges"]

# Create model
m = gp.Model("ring_routing")
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Decision variables
# Q[p,t]: production quantity
Q = m.addVars(products, range(T), lb=0, name="Q")

# I[p,l,t,r]: inventory at start of period t with r remaining life
I = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T + 1):  # Need T+1 for final state
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# sales[p,l,t,r]: sales from inventory with r remaining life
sales = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# W[p,l,t]: waste
W = m.addVars(products, locations, range(T), lb=0, name="W")

# lost_sales[p,l,t]: unmet demand
lost_sales = m.addVars(products, locations, range(T), lb=0, name="lost_sales")

# trans[p,l1,l2,t,r]: transshipment along ring edges
trans = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in range(T):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                trans[p, l1, l2, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"trans_{p}_{l1}_{l2}_{t}_{r}")

# sub[p1,p2,l,t]: substitution (p1 substitutes for p2)
sub = {}
for (p1, p2) in sub_edges:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            sub[p1, p2, l, t] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sub_{p1}_{p2}_{l}_{t}")

# Helper: get inbound/outbound edges for each location
inbound = {l: [] for l in locations}
outbound = {l: [] for l in locations}
for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
    outbound[l1].append((l1, l2))
    inbound[l2].append((l1, l2))

# Constraints

# Initial inventory is zero at t=0
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, sl + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in range(T):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] at start of period t comes from production distributed
# But we need to track: at END of period t, fresh goods arrive for period t+1
# Actually, let's reinterpret: Q[p,t] produces goods that are available at start of period t
# with full shelf life SL[p]

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            # Inbound transshipments with freshest life
            inbound_fresh = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, sl] for (l1, l2) in inbound[l])
            outbound_fresh = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, sl] for (l1, l2) in outbound[l])
            
            if t == 0:
                # First period: fresh inventory comes only from production
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l],
                    name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}"
                )
            else:
                # Fresh inventory = production share + inbound - outbound (for freshest)
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l] + inbound_fresh - outbound_fresh,
                    name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}"
                )

# Aging constraints: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] + inbound - outbound
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            for r in range(1, sl):  # r from 1 to SL-1
                inbound_trans = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, r + 1] for (l1, l2) in inbound[l])
                outbound_trans = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, r + 1] for (l1, l2) in outbound[l])
                
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] + inbound_trans - outbound_trans,
                    name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] (items with r=1 that aren't sold)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            # Account for transshipments of expiring items
            inbound_exp = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, 1] for (l1, l2) in inbound[l])
            outbound_exp = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, 1] for (l1, l2) in outbound[l])
            m.addConstr(
                W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] + inbound_exp - outbound_exp,
                name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r],
                    name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Transshipment availability: can only ship what you have minus what you sell
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                outbound_r = gp.quicksum(trans[p, l1, l2, t, r] for (l1, l2) in outbound[l])
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] + outbound_r <= I[p, l, t, r],
                    name=f"trans_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Demand satisfaction with substitution
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1))
            
            # Substitution: p can receive from products that substitute for it
            sub_received = gp.quicksum(sub[p1, p, l, t] for (p1, p2) in sub_edges if p2 == p)
            # Substitution: p can give to products it substitutes for
            sub_given = gp.quicksum(sub[p, p2, l, t] for (p1, p2) in sub_edges if p1 == p)
            
            m.addConstr(
                total_sales + sub_received + lost_sales[p, l, t] == local_demand + sub_given,
                name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Substitution limit: can only substitute from available inventory
for (p1, p2) in sub_edges:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T):
            total_sales_p1 = gp.quicksum(sales[p1, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p1] + 1))
            total_inv_p1 = gp.quicksum(I[p1, l, t, r] for r in range(1, shelf_life[p1] + 1))
            m.addConstr(
                total_sales_p1 + sub[p1, p2, l, t] <= total_inv_p1,
                name=f"sub_limit_{p1}_{p2}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in range(T):
        total_storage = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * I[p, l, t, r]
            for p in products
            for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
        )
        m.addConstr(total_storage <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"storage_{l}_{t}")

# Objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t]
    for p in products for t in range(T)
)

# Holding cost: charged on end-of-period inventory (I - sales) for r >= 2
holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r])
    for p in products
    for l in locations
    for t in range(T)
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t]
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(T)
)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["lost_sales"][p] * lost_sales[p, l, t]
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(T)
)

transshipment_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["transshipment"] * trans[p, l1, l2, t, r]
    for p in products
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges
    for t in range(T)
    for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(
    purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transshipment_cost,
    GRB.MINIMIZE
)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```

## Problem
[SCENARIO]
Family: F7 (Network and Multi Echelon)
Archetype: retail_f7_transshipment
Scenario ID: retail_f7_transshipment_v0

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB

# Data is pre-defined in 'data' variable

# Extract parameters
periods = data["periods"]
products = ["SKU_Basic", "SKU_Premium", "SKU_ShortLife"]
locations = ["DC1", "DC2", "DC3", "DC4", "DC5"]

shelf_life = {

    "SKU_Premium": data["shelf_life_sku_premium"],

}

    "DC1": data["cold_capacity_dc1"],
    "DC2": data["cold_capacity_dc2"],
    "DC3": data["cold_capacity_dc3"],
    "DC4": data["cold_capacity_dc4"],
    "DC5": data["cold_capacity_dc5"]
}

cold_usage = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["cold_usage_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["cold_usage_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["cold_usage_sku_shortlife"]
}

production_cap = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["production_cap_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["production_cap_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["production_cap_sku_shortlife"]
}

demand_curve = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["demand_curve_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["demand_curve_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["demand_curve_sku_shortlife"]
}

demand_share = {
    "DC1": data["demand_share_dc1"],
    "DC2": data["demand_share_dc2"],
    "DC3": data["demand_share_dc3"],
    "DC4": data["demand_share_dc4"],
    "DC5": data["demand_share_dc5"]
}

lost_sales_cost = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["lost_sales_cost_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["lost_sales_cost_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["lost_sales_cost_sku_shortlife"]
}

inventory_cost = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["inventory_cost_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["inventory_cost_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["inventory_cost_sku_shortlife"]
}

waste_cost = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["waste_cost_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["waste_cost_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["waste_cost_sku_shortlife"]
}

purchasing_cost = {
    "SKU_Basic": data["purchasing_cost_sku_basic"],
    "SKU_Premium": data["purchasing_cost_sku_premium"],
    "SKU_ShortLife": data["purchasing_cost_sku_shortlife"]
}

transshipment_cost = data["transshipment_cost"]

# Transshipment edges (full network)
trans_edges = [(l1, l2) for l1 in locations for l2 in locations if l1 != l2]

# Create model
m = gp.Model("retail_transshipment")
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Decision variables
# Q[p,t]: production quantity
Q = m.addVars(products, range(periods), lb=0, name="Q")

# I[p,l,t,r]: inventory at start of period t with r periods remaining
I = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods + 1):  # Need t+1 for aging constraints
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# sales[p,l,t,r]: sales from inventory with r periods remaining
sales = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# W[p,l,t]: waste
W = m.addVars(products, locations, range(periods), lb=0, name="W")

# L[p,l,t]: lost sales
L = m.addVars(products, locations, range(periods), lb=0, name="L")

# T[p,l1,l2,t,r]: transshipment from l1 to l2 for product p with remaining life r
T = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                T[p, l1, l2, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"T_{p}_{l1}_{l2}_{t}_{r}")

# Constraints

# Initial inventory is zero (t=0)
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, sl + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_inv_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
# This is the inventory at START of period t with freshest life
# But we need to account for transshipments within the period
# Re-reading: the fresh inflow is ONLY from production, transshipments are separate

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            # Fresh inventory at start of period comes from production
            # Transshipments happen during the period and affect what's available for sales
            m.addConstr(
                I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l],
                name=f"fresh_inflow_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Available inventory for sales/transshipment = I + incoming trans - outgoing trans
# sales + outgoing trans <= I + incoming trans

for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                trans_in = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                trans_out = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] + trans_out <= I[p, l, t, r] + trans_in,
                    name=f"avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] - trans_out + trans_in for r=1..SL-1
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl):  # r goes from 1 to SL-1
                # Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining
                # minus sales, minus outgoing trans, plus incoming trans
                trans_in = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r + 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                trans_out = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r + 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] - trans_out + trans_in,
                    name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] - trans_out + trans_in (for r=1)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            trans_in = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            trans_out = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            m.addConstr(
                W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] - trans_out + trans_in,
                name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# (5) Demand satisfaction: sum_r sales[p,l,t,r] + L[p,l,t] = demand[p,t] * share[l]
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(
                total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand,
                name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# (6) Cold capacity: sum_p cold_use[p] * end_of_period_inventory <= cold_cap[l]
# End of period inventory = I - sales - trans_out + trans_in (for r >= 2, since r=1 becomes waste)
for l in locations:
    for t in range(periods):
        end_inv = gp.LinExpr()
        for p in products:
            sl = shelf_life[p]
            for r in range(2, sl + 1):  # Exclude r=1 (becomes waste)
                trans_in = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                trans_out = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                end_inv += cold_usage[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] - trans_out + trans_in)
        m.addConstr(end_inv <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"cold_cap_{l}_{t}")

# (7) Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in range(periods):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# Objective: minimize total cost
obj = gp.LinExpr()

# Purchasing cost
for p in products:
    for t in range(periods):
        obj += purchasing_cost[p] * Q[p, t]

# Holding cost (on end-of-period inventory for r >= 2)
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(2, sl + 1):
                trans_in = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                trans_out = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                obj += inventory_cost[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] - trans_out + trans_in)

# Waste cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            obj += waste_cost[p] * W[p, l, t]

# Lost sales cost
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            obj += lost_sales_cost[p] * L[p, l, t]

# Transshipment cost
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                obj += transshipment_cost * T[p, l1, l2, t, r]

m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

# Optimize
m.optimize()

# Output
print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```

Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)

- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.

2. Aging for r = 1 to SL-1:
   I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] + net_transshipment[p,l,t,r+1]

3. Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] + net_transshipment_in[p,l,t,1]

4. Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] ≤ I[p,l,t,r] + inbound_trans[p,l,t,r] - outbound_trans[p,l,t,r]

5. Demand satisfaction: sum over r of sales[p,l,t,r] + L[p,l,t] = demand[p,t] * demand_share[l]

6. Production capacity: Q[p,t] ≤ production_cap[p,t]

7. Cold storage: sum over p,r of cold_usage[p] * (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r] + net_trans) ≤ cold_capacity[l]

import gurobipy as gp
from gurobipy import GRB
import json

# Data is pre-defined
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
T = data["periods"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
cost_purchasing = data["cost_purchasing"]
cost_inventory = data["cost_inventory"]
cost_waste = data["cost_waste"]
cost_lost_sales = data["cost_lost_sales"]
cost_transshipment = data["cost_transshipment"]

# Create model
m = gp.Model()
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Index sets
periods = range(T)
trans_edges = [(locations[i], locations[j]) for i in range(len(locations)) for j in range(len(locations)) if i != j]

# Decision variables
# Q[p,t]: production quantity
Q = m.addVars(products, periods, lb=0, name="Q")

# I[p,l,t,r]: inventory at start of period t with r periods remaining
I = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# sales[p,l,t,r]: sales from inventory with r remaining
sales = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# W[p,l,t]: waste
W = m.addVars(products, locations, periods, lb=0, name="W")

# L[p,l,t]: lost sales
L = m.addVars(products, locations, periods, lb=0, name="L")

# Trans[p,l1,l2,t,r]: transshipment from l1 to l2
Trans = {}
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                Trans[p, l1, l2, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"Trans_{p}_{l1}_{l2}_{t}_{r}")

m.update()

# Constraints

# Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, SL] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l], name=f"fresh_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Inventory aging with transshipment
# For t < T-1: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] + inbound_trans - outbound_trans
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(T - 1):
            for r in range(1, SL):  # r goes from 1 to SL-1
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l2, l, t, r + 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r + 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] + inbound - outbound,
                    name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] + inbound_trans - outbound_trans (for r=1)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l2, l, t, 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, 1] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            m.addConstr(
                W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] + inbound - outbound,
                name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r] + inbound - outbound
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r] + inbound - outbound,
                    name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Transshipment outbound limit: can't ship more than available
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, SL + 1):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                m.addConstr(outbound <= I[p, l, t, r], name=f"trans_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

# Demand satisfaction: sum of sales + lost sales = demand
for p in products:
    SL = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, SL + 1))
            m.addConstr(total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand, name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}")

# Cold storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        # End of period inventory = I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r] + net_trans for r >= 2
        # Plus waste items (r=1) don't count as they're disposed
        storage_used = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * (
                I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] 
                + gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
                - gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
            )
            for p in products
            for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
        )
        m.addConstr(storage_used <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"cold_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Objective: minimize total cost
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_inventory[p] * (
        I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]
        + gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l2, l, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
        - gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if l2 != l)
    )
    for p in products
    for l in locations
    for t in periods
    for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_waste[p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

transshipment_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_transshipment * Trans[p, l1, l2, t, r]
    for p in products
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges
    for t in periods
    for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transshipment_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```

Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2

- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

L = m.addVars(products, locations, periods, lb=0, name="L")

# T[p,l1,l2,t,r]: transshipment of product p with remaining life r from l1 to l2 in period t
T = {}
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                T[p, l1, l2, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"T_{p}_{l1}_{l2}_{t}_{r}")

# Constraints

# Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in periods:
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t], name=f"prod_cap_{p}_{t}")

# Initial inventory at t=0: Fresh inflow from production
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        # Fresh inventory (r = sl) at t=0 comes from production
        m.addConstr(
            I[p, l, 0, sl] == Q[p, 0] * demand_share[l],
            name=f"init_fresh_{p}_{l}"
        )
        # No older inventory at t=0
        for r in range(1, sl):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0, name=f"init_zero_{p}_{l}_{r}")

# Inventory dynamics for t >= 1
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(1, num_periods):
            # Fresh inflow (r = sl): from production
            m.addConstr(
                I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l],
                name=f"fresh_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )
            
            # Aging: I[p,l,t,r] = I[p,l,t-1,r+1] - sales[p,l,t-1,r+1] + net_transshipment
            for r in range(1, sl):
                inbound = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t-1, r+1] for (l2, l_dest) in trans_edges if l_dest == l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t-1, r+1] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l)
                m.addConstr(
                    I[p, l, t, r] == I[p, l, t-1, r+1] - sales[p, l, t-1, r+1] + inbound - outbound,
                    name=f"aging_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Waste: items with r=1 that aren't sold or transshipped
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            outbound_r1 = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, 1] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l)
            m.addConstr(
                W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] - outbound_r1,
                name=f"waste_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Sales availability: can only sell what's available after transshipments
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                inbound = gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for (l2, l_dest) in trans_edges if l_dest == l)
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l)
                m.addConstr(
                    sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r] + inbound - outbound,
                    name=f"sales_avail_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Transshipment outbound limit: can't ship more than available
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l)
                m.addConstr(
                    outbound <= I[p, l, t, r],
                    name=f"trans_limit_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}"
                )

# Demand satisfaction
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in periods:
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            m.addConstr(
                total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand,
                name=f"demand_{p}_{l}_{t}"
            )

# Cold storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in periods:
        # End-of-period inventory (after sales, before waste removal for r>=2)
        storage_used = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] 
                           + gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for (l2, l_dest) in trans_edges if l_dest == l)
                           - gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l))
            for p in products
            for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
        )
        m.addConstr(storage_used <= cold_capacity[l], name=f"cold_cap_{l}_{t}")

# Objective: minimize total cost
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_purchasing[p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in periods)

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_inventory[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]
                        + gp.quicksum(T[p, l2, l, t, r] for (l2, l_dest) in trans_edges if l_dest == l)
                        - gp.quicksum(T[p, l, l2, t, r] for (l_src, l2) in trans_edges if l_src == l))
    for p in products for l in locations for t in periods for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_waste[p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(cost_lost_sales[p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in periods)

transshipment_cost = gp.quicksum(
    cost_transshipment * T[p, l1, l2, t, r]
    for p in products for (l1, l2) in trans_edges for t in periods for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transshipment_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```

[SCENARIO]
Family: F7 (Network and Multi Echelon)
Archetype: retail_f7_transshipment
Scenario ID: retail_f7_transshipment_v4

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

[BUSINESS DESCRIPTION]
Business narrative:
The retailer operates a fully connected lateral transshipment network among all locations. Inventory can be moved between any pair of locations at a transshipment cost, allowing local surpluses to be reallocated to locations facing shortages. Demand remains local and exogenous at each site, and unsatisfied demand after considering local stock and inbound transshipments is lost and penalized.

Structure cues:
- This archetype extends the single-echelon inventory model by allowing transshipment flows along directed edges given in the JSON; in this case, all ordered pairs of distinct locations are connected (full network).
- Shelf life: Each product has a shelf life in periods. Inventory must be tracked by REMAINING LIFE.

  VARIABLE DEFINITION: I[p,l,t,r] = inventory at START of period t with r periods remaining.
  Convention: r=1 is OLDEST (sell first FIFO), r=shelf_life[p] is FRESHEST.

  KEY EQUATIONS - implement EXACTLY as written, do NOT add or remove terms:

  (1) Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
      - This is ONLY the inflow from production. Do NOT subtract sales here!
      - Q is total production, demand_share distributes it to locations.

  (2) Aging: I[p,l,t+1,r] = I[p,l,t,r+1] - sales[p,l,t,r+1] for r=1..SL-1
      - Inventory tomorrow with r remaining = inventory today with r+1 remaining - sales

  (3) Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1]
      - Items with r=1 that aren't sold become waste

  (4) Sales availability: sales[p,l,t,r] <= I[p,l,t,r]
      - Can only sell what you have in inventory

  (5) Inventory holding cost: charged on (I[p,l,t,r] - sales[p,l,t,r]) for r >= 2
      - Charge on END-of-period inventory (after sales), exclude expiring items (r=1)
- Storage capacity: sum over products of (cold_usage[p] * total_inventory[p,l,t]) <= cold_capacity[l]. These limits must be respected at each location.
- For each product and period, inventory at a location changes according to incoming production, incoming transshipments, outgoing transshipments, sales, and waste, and must remain non-negative.
- Transshipment flows from a location in a period cannot exceed that location's available inventory for the product. All such moves incur transshipment costs as specified in the JSON.
- Demand remains local: each location's demand must be met from its own on-hand inventory and inbound transshipments, if available.
- Lead times for transshipment are effectively zero in this archetype, so shipments dispatched in a period are available at the destination within the same period.
- The objective is to minimize total cost including purchasing, holding, waste, lost sales, and transshipment costs.

  "network": {"sub_edges": [["SKU_Basic", "SKU_Premium"]], "trans_edges": [["DC1","DC2"],["DC1","DC3"],["DC1","DC4"],["DC1","DC5"],["DC2","DC1"],["DC2","DC3"],["DC2","DC4"],["DC2","DC5"],["DC3","DC1"],["DC3","DC2"],["DC3","DC4"],["DC3","DC5"],["DC4","DC1"],["DC4","DC2"],["DC4","DC3"],["DC4","DC5"],["DC5","DC1"],["DC5","DC2"],["DC5","DC3"],["DC5","DC4"]]}
}
"""

data = json.loads(json_data)

periods = data["periods"]
products = data["products"]
locations = data["locations"]
shelf_life = data["shelf_life"]
cold_capacity = data["cold_capacity"]
cold_usage = data["cold_usage"]
production_cap = data["production_cap"]
demand_curve = data["demand_curve"]
demand_share = data["demand_share"]
costs = data["costs"]
trans_edges = data["network"]["trans_edges"]

m = gp.Model("retail_transshipment")
m.Params.OutputFlag = 0
m.Params.Threads = 1
m.Params.Seed = 0

# Decision variables
Q = {}  # Production
for p in products:
    for t in range(periods):
        Q[p, t] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"Q_{p}_{t}")

I = {}  # Inventory by remaining life
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods + 1):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                I[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"I_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

sales = {}  # Sales by remaining life
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                sales[p, l, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"sales_{p}_{l}_{t}_{r}")

W = {}  # Waste
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            W[p, l, t] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"W_{p}_{l}_{t}")

L = {}  # Lost sales
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            L[p, l, t] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"L_{p}_{l}_{t}")

Trans = {}  # Transshipment by remaining life
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for (l1, l2) in trans_edges:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                Trans[p, l1, l2, t, r] = m.addVar(lb=0, name=f"Trans_{p}_{l1}_{l2}_{t}_{r}")

# Constraints

# Initial inventory is zero
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for r in range(1, sl + 1):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, 0, r] == 0)

# Production capacity
for p in products:
    for t in range(periods):
        m.addConstr(Q[p, t] <= production_cap[p][t])

# Fresh inflow: I[p,l,t,SL] = Q[p,t] * demand_share[l]
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            m.addConstr(I[p, l, t, sl] == Q[p, t] * demand_share[l])

# Aging with transshipment for r = 1 to SL-1
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r + 1] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l1, l, t, r + 1] for l1 in locations if (l1, l) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                m.addConstr(I[p, l, t + 1, r] == I[p, l, t, r + 1] - sales[p, l, t, r + 1] - outbound + inbound)

# Waste: W[p,l,t] = I[p,l,t,1] - sales[p,l,t,1] - outbound + inbound (for r=1)
for p in products:
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, 1] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
            inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l1, l, t, 1] for l1 in locations if (l1, l) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
            m.addConstr(W[p, l, t] == I[p, l, t, 1] - sales[p, l, t, 1] - outbound + inbound)

# Sales availability: can only sell what's available after transshipment
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                inbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l1, l, t, r] for l1 in locations if (l1, l) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                m.addConstr(sales[p, l, t, r] <= I[p, l, t, r] - outbound + inbound)

# Transshipment availability: can only ship what you have
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            for r in range(1, sl + 1):
                outbound = gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                m.addConstr(outbound <= I[p, l, t, r])

# Demand satisfaction
for p in products:
    sl = shelf_life[p]
    for l in locations:
        for t in range(periods):
            total_sales = gp.quicksum(sales[p, l, t, r] for r in range(1, sl + 1))
            local_demand = demand_curve[p][t] * demand_share[l]
            m.addConstr(total_sales + L[p, l, t] == local_demand)

# Cold storage capacity
for l in locations:
    for t in range(periods):
        storage_used = gp.quicksum(
            cold_usage[p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r] 
                            - gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                            + gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l1, l, t, r] for l1 in locations if (l1, l) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges]))
            for p in products for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
        )
        m.addConstr(storage_used <= cold_capacity[l])

# Objective function
purchasing_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["purchasing"][p] * Q[p, t] for p in products for t in range(periods))

holding_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["inventory"][p] * (I[p, l, t, r] - sales[p, l, t, r]
                             - gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l, l2, t, r] for l2 in locations if (l, l2) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges])
                             + gp.quicksum(Trans[p, l1, l, t, r] for l1 in locations if (l1, l) in [(e[0], e[1]) for e in trans_edges]))
    for p in products for l in locations for t in range(periods) for r in range(2, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

waste_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["waste"][p] * W[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(periods))

lost_sales_cost = gp.quicksum(costs["lost_sales"][p] * L[p, l, t] for p in products for l in locations for t in range(periods))

transshipment_cost = gp.quicksum(
    costs["transshipment"] * Trans[p, l1, l2, t, r]
    for p in products for (l1, l2) in trans_edges for t in range(periods) for r in range(1, shelf_life[p] + 1)
)

m.setObjective(purchasing_cost + holding_cost + waste_cost + lost_sales_cost + transshipment_cost, GRB.MINIMIZE)

m.optimize()

print(f"status: {m.Status}")
if m.Status == 2:
    print(f"objective: {m.ObjVal}")
```
